title: El almuerzo del comedor
desc: Midday, a counter, and no menu anywhere
setting: It is noon, the comedor is full, and there are six pots on the counter with no names on them.

steps.speaker: Cocinera
steps.en: Afternoon. What shall I serve you?

options.feedback: There is no menu and there never will be. What is there today is the question that gets you the list.
You will get a plate, and it will be whatever she decides. Some days that is the better outcome.
The pots are the menu. Asking for paper marks you out before you have ordered.

steps.speaker: Cocinera
steps.es: Hay pollo, res y pescado. Con arroz y frijoles.
steps.en: There is chicken, beef and fish. With rice and beans.

options.es: Pollo, por favor. ¿Y me da ensalada?
options.en: Chicken, please. And could you give me salad?
options.feedback: Pick one and add the thing you want. The salad is usually cabbage with vinegar and it comes for nothing.
Clear enough. She is holding the spoon over four other pots waiting for you to say more.
There are nine people behind you. At midday the question is what, not how.

steps.speaker: Cocinera
steps.en: Shall I put plantain crisps or sweet plantain on it?

options.es: Maduro, por favor. Y un fresco de calala.
options.en: Sweet plantain, please. And a passion fruit drink.
options.feedback: You answered and ordered the drink in the same breath, which is what she was going to ask next anyway.
Correct. The drink is coming whether you order it or not, so you may as well choose it.
She will do it and charge you for it. It is not wrong, only more lunch than one person needs.

steps.speaker: Cocinera
steps.es: Son ochenta pesos. Siéntese, ya se lo llevo.
steps.en: That is eighty. Sit down, I will bring it over.

options.en: Thank you. Do I pay you now or afterwards?
options.feedback: It changes from place to place and asking costs nothing. In most comedores you pay when you leave.
Paying up front is never wrong. Her hands are full and she may wave you off until later.
A comedor lunch has a fixed price and nobody haggles over it. That is for the market, not for food on a plate.
